overview: These entries set how high the camera aims on a fighter you have locked on to.
description: Per-target lock-on camera tuning: the target character's Character.Id_CharacterCamera selects an FName-keyed row whose TargetHeightOffset is added to the target's foot/base Z to seed the lock-on gaze in camera modes 1-3. One 46-row retail export: 44 rows use 135.0 and CN_040/CN_240 use 200.0 Unreal world units (centimetres by engine convention).

ID.simple: The name the game uses to link a fighter to their lock-on camera setting.
ID.technical: FName at row +0x8, declared UPROPERTY(BlueprintReadWrite, EditAnywhere). The export declares ImportKeyField=Id and all 46 exported rows have row name == exported ID, but no traced C++ consumer reads the row's Id member as a value. UGameCharacterVirtualCamera::OnTargetChanged instead takes CameraId from the target's cached Character row Id_CharacterCamera (row +0xD8) and calls FindRow<FGameDataTableRow_CharacterCamera>(CameraId, FString(), false) over DTM->CharacterCameraDataTables (+0x460), so the DataTable row name is the effective lookup key and the first matching table wins. AGameCharacter::ResolveDataRows caches the selected Character row pointer (+0x3A0) during setup; no variation, mission override or camera-specific override rewrites Id_CharacterCamera. Alias Character rows share rows (CN_041->CN_040, CN_071->CN_070, CN_081->CN_080, CN_111->CN_110, CP_081->CP_080); CN_210 stores NAME_None and finds no row.

TargetHeightOffset.simple: How high above a locked-on fighter's feet the camera aims. A larger number raises the aim point.
TargetHeightOffset.technical: double at row +0x10, declared UPROPERTY(EditAnywhere) without BlueprintReadWrite. The reconstructed row constructor sets 0.0 (0.00f), but every exported row writes a value. OnTargetChanged starts a 0.25 s view blend, sets LockOnTargetIndex to the target's character index, and copies the first matching row's TargetHeightOffset into the cached LockOnGazeHeight (+0x398, member default 135.0); NAME_None or a miss writes the 135.0 .data fallback. Its invalid-target branch also writes 135.0, but the only two callers (camera modes 1 and 2) invoke it only for a valid target. CopyCameraStateFrom copies the cached height on character swap. The value is added without scaling to GAISlot014_LocationLike().Z, which is actor Z minus scaled capsule half-height: mode 1 seeds the gaze before SolveTargetCamera (gaze direction/2D distance, then the solver rewrites LockOnGazeLocation to the pivot), mode 2 sets the target-relative gaze every frame while a target is valid, and entering mode 3 adds it to a valid target's base Z and derives LockOnHeightDifference; subsequent mode-3 updates use Mode3GazeLocation instead. No other C++ read of LockOnHeightDifference was found. Export values are 135.0 in 44 rows and 200.0 in CN_040 and CN_240.

notes: The retail export is one DataTable named CharacterCameraDataTable (RowStruct GameDataTableRow_CharacterCamera, ImportKeyField=Id) with 46 rows and no duplicate keys: 44 x TargetHeightOffset=135.0, CN_040=200.0, CN_240=200.0. All 46 datatables_by_character/*/CharacterCameraDataTable.json shards contain exactly the matching single row and agree with the master export.

The camera row belongs to the lock-on target, not to the camera owner. Cross-referencing all 48 CharacterDataTable rows shows every non-None Id_CharacterCamera resolves to one of the 46 camera rows, no camera row is unreferenced, five alias rows share a target row (CN_041->CN_040, CN_071->CN_070, CN_081->CN_080, CN_111->CN_110, CP_081->CP_080), and CN_210 uses NAME_None so it receives the 135.0 fallback.

AGameDataTableManager creates one primary-asset loader named CharacterCameraDataTable, waits until every DataTable loader has completed, resolves the UDataTable through the asset manager, and appends it to CharacterCameraDataTables (DTM +0x460). FindRow loops that array in order and returns on the first match; there is no duplicate-key preference logic. The per-character shard files are export views, not separately loaded assets.

OnTargetChanged is called only from camera modes 1 and 2, only when the target's CharacterIndex differs from the cached LockOnTargetIndex (initial sentinel 0xFF). Mode 3 never calls it. Repointing a live target's camera row or changing its Character row without changing that index does not refresh LockOnGazeHeight until a qualifying target change or camera-state copy.

The reconstructed default 0.0 row value is not observed in the export. The 135.0 fallback equals the normal exported value, so a missing/None camera reference is data-visible only through the Character.Id_CharacterCamera join, not through a distinct height.

The similarly named GameDebugManager::CameraTargetHeightOffset is a separate float debug value (default 150.0), written by the debug slider; no C++ read of it or of its changed flag was found, and it is not this table's value or the 135.0 fallback.

Evidence is reconstructed C++ annotated with retail RVAs (including behaviour-certified OnTargetChanged and mode-2/3 functions in this checkout) plus the community retail DataTable exports. No retail Blueprint graph or live runtime was inspected, so Blueprint-only consumers or editor-side overrides cannot be excluded; no byte-identical source or playtest claim is made.

usages.detail: Registers CharacterCameraDataTable in the list used to create DataTable primary-asset loaders.
Creates the loader map from the registered primary-asset names.
Defers table-array population until all DataTable loaders report completion.
Resolves the single CharacterCameraDataTable UDataTable and appends it to CharacterCameraDataTables (DTM +0x460).
Caches the resolved selected Character row pointer used later to obtain Id_CharacterCamera.
Reads Id_CharacterCamera from the locked-on target's cached Character row.
Finds the first CharacterCamera row whose row name matches that FName; falls back to 135.0 on a miss.
Copies TargetHeightOffset into the cached LockOnGazeHeight.
Mode 1: initial lock-on gaze = target foot/base location plus LockOnGazeHeight.
Mode 1: SolveTargetCamera uses the offset-seeded gaze for direction/pitch and rewrites the gaze location to the solved pivot.
Mode 2: per-frame lock-on gaze = target foot/base location plus LockOnGazeHeight.
Mode 3 entry: adds LockOnGazeHeight to a valid target's foot/base Z to initialize LockOnGazeLocation.
Mode 3 entry: derives LockOnHeightDifference from the offset gaze and the owner's eye base.
Mode 3 updates use Mode3GazeLocation directly; they do not reread LockOnGazeHeight.
Character swap copies the cached LockOnGazeHeight into the new virtual camera.
